name: Dual-Operator Nonlocal F+ with Off-Ray Kinetic-Isolated Khronon Frame (DOKF)
claimed_mechanism: This architecture decouples the MOND force-law nonlocality from the preferred-frame lensing slip. The MOND constraint is satisfied by an auxiliary scalar chi coupled to the matter density via a spatially nonlocal elliptic kernel, satisfying the scale-split theorem by using an independent auxiliary scalar s to gap the propagating mode. A standard-kinetic timelike vector u_mu provides the necessary off-ray lensing slip required by DC-013, but its PPN-visible coupling to acceleration is screened by e^-y, ensuring the Solar System is decoupled from the preferred frame.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the theory recovers GR with MOND-enhanced dynamics. The spatially nonlocal kernel generates the correct MOND force law at galactic scales, while the localized extra mode is gapped at a scale short of the MOND kernel's range. The preferred-frame vector u_mu mediates the lensing slip, with its PPN parameters (alpha_1, alpha_2) vanishing as e^-y in the high-acceleration limit, ensuring no strong-coupling divergence in the Solar System.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-010 (finite-alpha_inf khronometric MOND) because it does not rely on a khronon field with a fixed background; instead, it uses a standard-kinetic vector whose PPN coupling is dynamically screened by e^-y. It is inequivalent to DC-014 (stiff/non-propagating screened preferred-frame vector) because the vector u_mu has standard kinetic normalization, not degenerate or stiff, avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wall. It is inequivalent to DC-001 (local no-preferred-frame lensing MOND) because it explicitly includes a preferred-frame vector, which is required for correct MOND lensing. It is inequivalent to DC-012 (frameless localized-nonlocal MOND) because it includes a preferred-frame carrier, evading the slip-lock theorem.
